evidence.observation: The plan says, "A failure before evaluation must never look like an empty successful check," but its intake cases name only "raw schemas 7, 12 and 14" and "A missing population exits 3 with zero failed constraints."

concerns.recommendation: Specify the status and diagnostics when an outer envelope reports failure while an inner report appears successful, and when a supported wrapper lacks or corrupts its inner report. Assert that neither case yields an empty successful verdict.
concerns.title: Outer failure precedence has no conflicting-envelope acceptance case

evidence.observation: PS1 promises to "expose the CLI vacuity acceptance option to Python" and document "empty and missing coverage," but §9 gives no expected results for vacuity combined with a failed or indeterminate verdict.

concerns.recommendation: Add cases for complete empty participation, missing coverage, and a vacuous constraint alongside a failure or indeterminate constraint. Assert that opting into vacuity changes only the vacuous outcome and preserves the higher-priority result.
concerns.title: Vacuity opt-in could mask another check outcome

evidence.observation: PS2 must "Distinguish a complete empty extension from one that could not be computed," while its acceptance check says only to "Exercise a redacted role and a capped extension."

concerns.recommendation: Define per-request availability when a row or byte cap interrupts an extension. Test complete empty, unavailable, and capped partial results against a known extension; assert the returned rows and findings stay within their limits and that the evaluation count is one.
concerns.title: A capped extension has no specified completeness signal

evidence.observation: PS3 says, "Replay a fully grounded negative premise only with covered relations," but the stated check is only to "invalidate a negative witness when the blocked relation changes."

concerns.recommendation: Use two positive bindings that assign different values to a variable read by the negative premise, with the negated relation matching only one value. Reverse row order, then remove coverage; assert binding-specific replay and an unavailable result when coverage is absent.
concerns.title: Negation replay is untested for correlated bindings and absent coverage

evidence.observation: The plan promises "per-target work and exhaustion," yet its PS3 acceptance case only replays "two targets against one loaded snapshot."

concerns.recommendation: Make one target exhaust its work limit and a second complete under the same loaded snapshot; reverse their order. Assert each target's status and counters independently, while checking that shared snapshot loading occurs once.
concerns.title: Batch acceptance does not prove per-target budget isolation

evidence.observation: PS4 promises "model invalidation" and a "versioned persistent local worker," but its exercise is "two requests in one isolated process, force one invalid input, then evaluate a valid request; log request IDs, model identities and restart behavior."

concerns.recommendation: Specify the invalidation key and recovery behavior. Compare worker results with fresh in-process evaluation after changing model bytes at the same path and after a worker crash or timeout; verify that no prior request's model, population, or disclosure state appears in the next response.
concerns.title: Valid-after-invalid requests do not establish worker invalidation or crash recovery

response.summary: The planned acceptance checks leave six observable contract gaps across envelope handling, vacuity, extension availability, batch explanations, and worker recovery.
